questions.stem: A clinician's note zooms the page to 200%; does a 200px width element change its CSS pixel width?

options.text: No, CSS pixels stay 200px; device pixels double

questions.explanation: Zoom changes device pixels, not CSS pixels. The declared 200px stays 200 CSS pixels. Converting or auto is wrong.

questions.stem: What is the specificity of :not(.active) in a clinician's note stylesheet?

questions.learningObjective: Handle margin collapse with border and padding
questions.stem: Explain why both border and padding on a parent prevent child margin collapse in a clinician's note.

answer.exemplar: Both border and padding create a physical boundary between the parent and child margins, so the child's margin cannot reach and collapse with the parent's margin or the parent's parent's margin.

questions.explanation: Border and padding each block collapse-through by separating margins. Either one suffices. They do not merge or convert margins.

options.text: It hides from assistive tech only
It only hides visually but keeps space
It applies display: none via user-agent stylesheet
It has no effect without CSS

questions.explanation: The hidden attribute maps to display: none in the user-agent stylesheet, removing the box. It is not visibility hidden or aria-hidden. It works without custom CSS.
